passages.text: But if, as you say, he is to be revealed to everyone now through Jesus for the sake of knowing him, how do you not call it most unjust that those men did not know him—seven pillars of the world who were able to please the most just God—while now so many from the nations, impious in every way, know him? Were those men not deemed worthy to know the one better than all? And how is what is not just good? Unless by good you wish to mean not the one who benefits those who have acted justly, but the one who loves the unrighteous even if they do not believe, revealing to them also the secrets that he was unwilling to reveal to the righteous. Such conduct belongs neither to a good nor to a just being, but to one who hates the reverent. Are you perhaps the standing one, Simon, who is so emboldened as to say that these things were spoken in a way they never were?

lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the stated seven without supplying an unprinted list of names.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μήτι σὺ εἶ, Σίμων, ὁ ἑστώς
lexical_decisions.chosen: Are you perhaps the standing one, Simon
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the standing epithet and interrogative challenge, not a translator’s identification of Simon.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰ δὲ (ὡς φῄς) ἔσται διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι διὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ νῦν πᾶσιν ἀποκαλύπτεσθαι:
lexical_decisions.chosen: But if, as you say, he is to be revealed to everyone now through Jesus for the sake of knowing him
lexical_decisions.rationale: Is to be retains future ἔσται while now retains νῦν. The main text construes διὰ τὸ εἰδέναι purposively, for the sake of knowing, with him supplied as the contextual object, the previously discussed Father. The causal alternative is because of knowing; the clause does not state whose prior knowledge would ground disclosure on that attachment. No claim is added that the revealed one was already known to everyone.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὗτοι παντὸς κρείττονος γνῶναι οὐ κατηξιώθησαν;
lexical_decisions.chosen: Were those men not deemed worthy to know the one better than all?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The context concerns knowing the proposed highest Father, favoring a personal referent superior to all and παντός as the comparison of κρείττονος. Taking παντός with substantival κρείττονος gives the broader alternative Were these not deemed worthy to know anything superior? The genitive superior object is construed with deemed worthy/knowing in this compressed phrase; the personal interpretation is not claimed as unique.

passages.text: Some sinned in this way from the supposition that, because of his goodness, he does not judge; others from the opposite view. For, supposing the statements of the scriptures against God to be true, although they are unjust and false, they did not know his true divinity and power. Therefore, supposing that he is ignorant, delights in murders, lets the wicked off through gifts of sacrifices, and also deceives, lies, and does everything unjust, they themselves, thinking they had acted like God, insisted while sinning that they were acting reverently. Therefore they were immovable toward what is better, and when admonished did not turn back. For they had no fear, considering themselves made like God through such actions.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰς γὰρ κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῶν γραφῶν φωνάς, ἀδίκους οὔσας καὶ ψευδεῖς
lexical_decisions.chosen: the statements of the scriptures against God ... although they are unjust and false
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the historical speaker’s explicit criticism of certain scriptural statements. It is neither softened nor presented as the translator’s own verdict about scripture.
Retains the turning verb distinct from μετανοέω/reorient.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐκ τῆς διὰ τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἀκρίτου ὑπολήψεως
lexical_decisions.chosen: from the supposition that, because of his goodness, he does not judge
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main text understands a supposition of God’s non-judging character, because 18.18 explicitly links presumed goodness with absence of pursuit of sins and judgment. Alternatively ἀκρίτου qualifies ὑπολήψεως: from the uncritical or unexamined supposition prompted by his goodness. On that attachment the adjective characterizes the supposition, not God’s judging activity. Neither reading is treated as a source defect.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: αὐτοὶ ὡς ὅμοια θεοῦ ποιήσαντες, ἁμαρτάνοντες ἰσχυρίζοντο εὐσεβεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: they themselves, thinking they had acted like God, insisted while sinning that they were acting reverently
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὡς presents the alleged imitation from their viewpoint, not a fact affirmed by the narrator, who just called the accusations about God false. Had acted retains the retrospective aorist participle, while thinking makes their rationale explicit.

passages.text: As Simon said this and was about to go out, Peter said, “Hear this further thing from me, then go wherever you wish.” Simon turned and remained, and Peter said, “I know how you were astounded then when you heard me say, ‘Whoever says anything against the God who created the world, I do not believe him.’ Now hear something greater than this. If the God who created the world really were in character such as the scriptures describe him, and even if in some other way he were incomparably evil, beyond what either the scriptures could say or anyone else could even conceive, I would nevertheless not stop revering him alone and doing his will. For I want you to know and be persuaded that the person who has no affection for his own maker can never have it for another either. If he does have it for another, he has it contrary to nature and does not know that he has from evil the love of the unjust, since he cannot even keep that love firm. And if there really is someone else above the maker, being good he will receive me all the more because I love my own Father; but he will not receive you, knowing that you abandoned your maker by nature—I do not say father—for a greater hope, without concern for what is reasonable. Thus, if you find someone superior even to him, he knows that you will abandon him too someday, especially since he has not become your father, when you have abandoned even your true father.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐὰν τῷ ὄντι ὁ τὸν κόσμον κτίσας θεὸς τὴν γνώμην τοιοῦτος ὢν τυγχάνῃ
lexical_decisions.chosen: If the God who created the world really were in character such as ...
lexical_decisions.rationale: The description is explicitly hypothetical. The severe conditional is preserved, not rewritten as an assertion that the maker is evil.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐκ πονηροῦ τὸν τῶν ἀδίκων ἔρωτα ἔχων
lexical_decisions.chosen: he has from evil the love of the unjust
lexical_decisions.rationale: From evil adopts the impersonal reading of πονηροῦ, since the immediate context does not identify a personal evil agent. From an evil one or the evil one is grammatically possible but is not asserted through imported theology. Love of the unjust may be love characteristic of unjust people or love directed toward them; the main phrase retains that ambiguity.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν φύσει σου ποιητὴν (οὐ γὰρ λέγω πατέρα)
lexical_decisions.chosen: your maker by nature—I do not say father
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves Peter’s pointed change from father to maker in addressing Simon rather than harmonizing all parent-language.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὕτως εἰ καὶ αὐτοῦ κρείττονα εὑρήσεις
lexical_decisions.chosen: Thus, if you find someone superior even to him
lexical_decisions.rationale: Superior retains broader comparative κρείττονα without specifying the basis of superiority. Better or stronger are material alternatives, but the argument about changing allegiances does not require strength alone.
